prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your exact location, budget, the size/age of your home, the system you want, and whether you want a specific brand or efficiency level. I can find highly rated local contractors for you if you tell me your ZIP code. Meanwhile, here’s a short, practical guide to help you choose the best company in Atlanta for replacing your air conditioner.

What I recommend you do
- Get at least 3 written estimates from different contractors (same scope of work for apples-to-apples comparison).  
- Make sure each contractor does a Manual J load calculation (not just “match the old unit”) to size the system properly.  
- Confirm licensing and insurance: ask for the contractor’s Georgia license number and proof of general liability insurance and workers’ comp.  
- Look for NATE-certified technicians and factory-authorized dealer status if you prefer a certain brand (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, etc.).  
- Check recent online reviews (Google, Yelp), BBB rating, and ask for local references you can contact.  
- Compare total cost, expected efficiency (SEER rating), warranties (equipment and labor), and what’s included (new pad, line set, thermostat, permit, disposal).  
- Ask who handles permits and inspections, and whether the quote includes permits.  
- Ask about ductwork inspection/repairs and indoor air quality options (filters, UV, humidifier).  
- Check for rebates or utility incentives and available financing.  

Red flags to avoid
- Extremely low estimate without a site visit.  
- No written contract or vague scope of work.  
- Refusal to provide license/insurance information.  
- No load calculation or undersized equipment.  
- Pressure to sign immediately or push for expensive add-ons without explanation.

If you want, I can:
- Pull up a list of top-rated HVAC companies near your address or ZIP code.  
- Compare 3 companies side-by-side (estimates, warranties, reviews) if you already have quotes.

Tell me your ZIP code and any preferences (brand, budget, timeline) and I’ll find 3 well-rated local contractors and summarize their pros/cons.
